results.name: repeated_set_exposure_residual_slope
results.description: Correlation between how many times a participant has previously seen the same number_set in their session and the response residual (rating minus the leave-one-out cell mean of other participants), among trials of sets the participant sees at least 5 times; observed below null means people narrow their generalisation (more no) as a set is re-encountered, above means they broaden — set-specific learning the stationary model lacks.
results.code:
# name: repeated_set_exposure_residual_slope
# description: Correlation between how many times a participant has previously seen the same number_set in their session and the response residual (rating minus the leave-one-out cell mean of other participants), among trials of sets the participant sees at least 5 times; observed below null means people narrow their generalisation (more no) as a set is re-encountered, above means they broaden — set-specific learning the stationary model lacks.
def test_statistic(df):
    ti = df["trial_index"].to_numpy()
    pid = np.cumsum(np.r_[0, np.diff(ti) < 0])
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    ns = df["number_set"].astype(str).to_numpy()
    cell = (df["number_set"].astype(str) + "|" + df["target"].astype(str)).to_numpy()
    g = pd.Series(y).groupby(cell)
    s = g.transform("sum").to_numpy(); c = g.transform("count").to_numpy()
    res = y - (s - y) / np.maximum(c - 1, 1)
    key = pd.Series(pid.astype(str)) + "#" + pd.Series(ns)
    k = pd.DataFrame({"key": key, "ti": ti}).sort_values(["key", "ti"])
    exp_ = k.groupby("key").cumcount().reindex(range(len(df))).to_numpy()
    tot = key.map(key.value_counts()).to_numpy()
    ok = (c > 1) & (tot >= 5)
    return float(np.corrcoef(np.log1p(exp_[ok]), res[ok])[0, 1])

results.name: unanimous_cell_fraction
results.description: Fraction of (number_set, target) cells answered by exactly 5 participants in which all 5 gave the same answer (all yes or all no); observed above null means human generalisation is more categorical/consensual (cell probabilities pushed to 0/1) than the model's graded predictions, below means people split more than predicted.
results.code:
# name: unanimous_cell_fraction
# description: Fraction of (number_set, target) cells answered by exactly 5 participants in which all 5 gave the same answer (all yes or all no); observed above null means human generalisation is more categorical/consensual (cell probabilities pushed to 0/1) than the model's graded predictions, below means people split more than predicted.
def test_statistic(df):
    cell = (df["number_set"].astype(str) + "|" + df["target"].astype(str)).to_numpy()
    g = df["rating"].astype(float).groupby(cell).agg(["sum", "count"])
    g = g[g["count"] == 5]
    return float(((g["sum"] == 0) | (g["sum"] == 5)).mean())

results.name: cross_trial_residual_carryover
results.description: Within-participant lag-1 correlation of response residuals (rating minus the leave-one-out cell mean of other participants on the same number_set and target) between consecutive trials, regardless of whether the set changed; observed above null means a yes on one trial makes the next trial's answer more yes than its stimulus warrants (sequential assimilation the stateless model lacks), below means contrast/alternation.
results.code:
# name: cross_trial_residual_carryover
# description: Within-participant lag-1 correlation of response residuals (rating minus the leave-one-out cell mean of other participants on the same number_set and target) between consecutive trials, regardless of whether the set changed; observed above null means a yes on one trial makes the next trial's answer more yes than its stimulus warrants (sequential assimilation the stateless model lacks), below means contrast/alternation.
def test_statistic(df):
    ti = df["trial_index"].to_numpy()
    pid = np.cumsum(np.r_[0, np.diff(ti) < 0])
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    cell = (df["number_set"].astype(str) + "|" + df["target"].astype(str)).to_numpy()
    g = pd.Series(y).groupby(cell)
    s = g.transform("sum").to_numpy(); c = g.transform("count").to_numpy()
    res = np.where(c > 1, y - (s - y) / np.maximum(c - 1, 1), np.nan)
    a, b = res[:-1], res[1:]
    ok = (np.diff(pid) == 0) & np.isfinite(a) & np.isfinite(b)
    return float(np.corrcoef(a[ok], b[ok])[0, 1])

results.name: participant_discrimination_spread
results.description: Standard deviation across participants (450-trial blocks) of the correlation between a participant's responses and the leave-one-out mean response of the other participants on the same (number_set, target) cell; observed above null means participants differ in how closely they follow the shared generalisation pattern (individual differences in strategy or attentiveness the pooled model lacks), below means more uniform than predicted.
results.code:
# name: participant_discrimination_spread
# description: Standard deviation across participants (450-trial blocks) of the correlation between a participant's responses and the leave-one-out mean response of the other participants on the same (number_set, target) cell; observed above null means participants differ in how closely they follow the shared generalisation pattern (individual differences in strategy or attentiveness the pooled model lacks), below means more uniform than predicted.
def test_statistic(df):
    ti = df["trial_index"].to_numpy()
    pid = np.cumsum(np.r_[0, np.diff(ti) < 0])
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    cell = (df["number_set"].astype(str) + "|" + df["target"].astype(str)).to_numpy()
    g = pd.Series(y).groupby(cell)
    s = g.transform("sum").to_numpy(); c = g.transform("count").to_numpy()
    ok = c > 1
    loo = (s - y) / np.maximum(c - 1, 1)
    t = pd.DataFrame({"p": pid[ok], "y": y[ok], "l": loo[ok]})
    t["yl"] = t.y * t.l; t["yy"] = t.y ** 2; t["ll"] = t.l ** 2
    a = t.groupby("p").mean()
    cov = a.yl - a.y * a.l
    sd = np.sqrt(np.maximum(a.yy - a.y ** 2, 1e-12) * np.maximum(a.ll - a.l ** 2, 1e-12))
    r = (cov / sd).to_numpy()
    return float(np.std(r))

results.name: participant_bias_spread
results.description: Standard deviation across the 15 participants (contiguous 450-trial blocks where trial_index restarts) of each participant's mean residual yes rate relative to the cell mean (same number_set and target, all participants); observed above null means stable individual differences in yes bias that the single pooled model cannot produce, below means people are more homogeneous than binomial noise.
results.code:
# name: participant_bias_spread
# description: Standard deviation across the 15 participants (contiguous 450-trial blocks where trial_index restarts) of each participant's mean residual yes rate relative to the cell mean (same number_set and target, all participants); observed above null means stable individual differences in yes bias that the single pooled model cannot produce, below means people are more homogeneous than binomial noise.
def test_statistic(df):
    ti = df["trial_index"].to_numpy()
    pid = np.cumsum(np.r_[0, np.diff(ti) < 0])
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    cell = df["number_set"].astype(str) + "|" + df["target"].astype(str)
    g = pd.Series(y).groupby(cell.to_numpy())
    s = g.transform("sum").to_numpy(); c = g.transform("count").to_numpy()
    ok = c > 1
    res = np.where(ok, y - (s - y) / np.maximum(c - 1, 1), np.nan)
    m = pd.Series(res).groupby(pid).mean()
    return float(np.nanstd(m.to_numpy()))

results.name: late_session_discrimination_change
results.description: Correlation between responses and the leave-one-out cell mean of other participants (same number_set and target) in the last third of each session (trial_index >= 300) minus the first third (trial_index < 150); observed below null means responses become noisier / less stimulus-driven late in the session (fatigue or lapses the stationary model lacks), above means people become more consistent with practice.
results.code:
# name: late_session_discrimination_change
# description: Correlation between responses and the leave-one-out cell mean of other participants (same number_set and target) in the last third of each session (trial_index >= 300) minus the first third (trial_index < 150); observed below null means responses become noisier / less stimulus-driven late in the session (fatigue or lapses the stationary model lacks), above means people become more consistent with practice.
def test_statistic(df):
    ti = df["trial_index"].to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    cell = (df["number_set"].astype(str) + "|" + df["target"].astype(str)).to_numpy()
    g = pd.Series(y).groupby(cell)
    s = g.transform("sum").to_numpy(); c = g.transform("count").to_numpy()
    ok = c > 1
    loo = (s - y) / np.maximum(c - 1, 1)
    early = ok & (ti < 150); late = ok & (ti >= 300)
    r1 = np.corrcoef(y[early], loo[early])[0, 1]
    r2 = np.corrcoef(y[late], loo[late])[0, 1]
    return float(r2 - r1)

results.name: single_square_example_square_target_yes
results.description: Yes rate for perfect-square targets (other than the example itself) on single-example sets whose example is a perfect square (4, 9, ..., 100); observed above null means people read a lone square as "squares" more readily than the model's equal familiar-rule prior allows (model under-produces), below means the model over-endorses the squares rule.

results.name: shared_units_digit_nonmatch_leakage
results.description: Yes rate for targets whose units digit differs from the examples' common units digit, among multi-example sets whose examples all end in the same digit; observed above null means people hedge beyond an "ends in d" reading (via ranges/similarity) more than the model predicts, i.e. the model commits too hard to the units-digit rule; below means people commit even more.
results.code:
# name: shared_units_digit_nonmatch_leakage
# description: Yes rate for targets whose units digit differs from the examples' common units digit, among multi-example sets whose examples all end in the same digit; observed above null means people hedge beyond an "ends in d" reading (via ranges/similarity) more than the model predicts, i.e. the model commits too hard to the units-digit rule; below means people commit even more.
def test_statistic(df):
    parts = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True)
    nums = parts.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    units = nums % 10
    n = nums.notna().sum(axis=1)
    umin = units.min(axis=1); umax = units.max(axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    m = (n >= 2) & (umin == umax) & ((t % 10) != umin)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df.loc[m, "rating"].astype(float).mean())
